definition: Estimating a camera’s position and orientation within a known map — a core component of visual SLAM and AR.
details: Estimating a camera’s position and orientation within a known map — a core component of visual SLAM and AR.

explainer.lead: Camera localization works out where a camera is and which way it is pointing by relating what it sees to a map that already exists. It gives visual SLAM and augmented reality the camera pose needed to interpret new images consistently with that map.

tiers.eli5: Imagine walking through a room with a map while looking through a camera. By comparing what you see with landmarks on the map, you can work out both where you are standing and which direction the camera is facing.
tiers.practitioner: A localization system takes the current camera image and a known map, then estimates a pose that places visual observations in the map. It can supply the camera state within a visual SLAM or AR pipeline. A useful diagnostic is to distinguish poor pose estimates from an inaccurate or outdated map, since localization assumes that the map is known.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a known map M and camera observations, camera localization estimates the pose T = (R, t), where R is orientation and t is position. Equivalently, it recovers the camera's six degrees of freedom: three for translation and three for rotation. Unlike full SLAM, the task presupposes M rather than requiring map estimation and localization together.

explainer.example: An AR phone has a known map of a living room and captures an image showing one wall and a corner of a table. Localization estimates that the phone is 1.5 metres from that wall and turned toward the table, allowing the AR system to place new camera views in the same room coordinates.

usedIn.name: Visual SLAM
usedIn.detail: Estimates the camera pose relative to the spatial map used by the system.

usedIn.name: Augmented reality
usedIn.detail: Provides the position and viewing direction needed to relate the camera view to a known environment.

explainer.intuition: A familiar scene looks different depending on where you stand and which way you look. Camera localization reverses that relationship: it uses the view and a known map to infer the viewpoint.
howItWorks: Start with the current camera image and an existing map.
Relate parts of the observed view to information in the map.
Estimate the camera position that best explains those relationships.
Estimate the camera orientation alongside its position.
Return the combined pose for use by visual SLAM or AR.
explainer.whyItMatters: Without a camera pose, observations cannot be placed consistently in the map's coordinate system. Reliable localization therefore underpins camera tracking in visual SLAM and stable spatial alignment in AR.
misconceptions: It is not just finding coordinates: orientation is part of the answer too.
It is not the same as building a map: camera localization starts with a known map.
It does not describe where objects are in an image; it describes the camera's pose in the map.

diagram.caption: Camera localization combines a current view with a known map to estimate position and orientation.
